conflicts.issue: Scope, Bylaws, and Public Messaging of the Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
conflicts.summary: During the six-month Task Force update, county commissioners and city officials clashed over whether task force members were exceeding their advisory mandate by organizing public opposition campaigns against the Youth Home and criticizing Bull City United staffing, versus fulfilling their charge to engage residents on non-carceral safety alternatives.
conflicts.side_a_position: Task Force members should adhere strictly to bylaws by submitting vetted formal recommendations to elected boards rather than running public advocacy campaigns or claiming BOCC failed to fund prevention leadership.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and Chair Brenda A. Howerton objected to public campaigns accusing commissioners of prioritizing youth 'cages' when BOCC already funded a CISS department director, data statistician, and My Brother's Keeper initiatives.

Commissioners and Council Member DeDreana Freeman cited a missing Q1 report, unclear board-liaison notification of public forums, and the need to respect bylaws limiting official action to recommendations.
conflicts.side_b_position: Task Force town halls, public dialogue, and critiques of Youth Home detention spending and BCU oversight reflect legitimate community-led exploration of non-carceral safety strategies.
side_b_arguments: Task Force Co-chair Marcia Owens questioned expanding Bull City United into more neighborhoods before hiring a dedicated director and voiced community concern over Youth Home funding.

Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson defended the task force's public town halls and focus on non-carceral recommendations, noting elected bodies retain final authority to adopt or reject proposals (while Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton urged an inclusive approach that does not exclude law enforcement).
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; committee members concluded discussion by emphasizing clearer liaison communication and submitting written recommendations to the City Council and BOCC in 2022.

conflicts.issue: Legality, Business Impact, and Preemption Risk of Proposed 10-Cent Single-Use Bag Fee
conflicts.summary: Committee members and stakeholders debated whether Durham City and County have statutory authority to enact a 10-cent carryout bag fee framed as a stormwater utility mitigation measure without triggering litigation or state legislative retaliation.
conflicts.side_a_position: Pursue a local 10-cent single-use bag fee using stormwater/solid-waste regulatory authority to cut plastic pollution and litter-cleanup costs.
side_a_arguments: Duke Environmental Law Clinic presented legal analysis distinguishing a targeted mitigation fee tied to stormwater/waste impacts from prohibited general sales taxes.
Environmental advocates and Mayor Schewel noted voluntary outreach has failed to curb bag litter and pointed to other jurisdictions' sharp reductions after bag fees.
conflicts.side_b_position: Question statutory authority under North Carolina preemption rules and warn against retail compliance burdens and General Assembly retaliation.
side_b_arguments: NC Retail Merchants Association argued NCGS 160A-215.1 bars local taxes on retail sales and said small and grocery retailers oppose mandated bag-fee administration.
DeDreana Freeman warned that testing state preemption boundaries with a bag fee could provoke the General Assembly into restricting Durham's existing local stormwater utility fee.
conflicts.resolution: Informational / Requested formal legal review from the City Attorney and County Attorney before advancing an ordinance

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the December 15, 2021 Joint City-County Committee meeting alongside Durham Mayor Elaine O'Neal, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, Council Member DeDreana Freeman, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, and Commissioner Nida Allam, with Commissioner Heidi Carter also attending. The committee unanimously approved its October 12, 2021 minutes (3-0 on the BOCC committee roll call; 6-0 combined with City members) and received an interlocal quarterly report from General Manager Joanne Pierce on Bull City United's expansion toward 25 positions across six census tracts under the new Community Intervention and Support Services (CISS) department. During the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force six-month update, commissioners and council members debated task force bylaws, missing quarterly reports, and public criticism surrounding the Youth Home. After postponing one item, the committee extended the session to receive a Durham Children's Initiative update on the community-led Early Childhood Action Plan before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Joint Committee Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the joint committee meeting and welcomed newly seated Durham Mayor Elaine O'Neal, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, and Council Member DeDreana Freeman alongside BOCC committee members Nida Allam, Wendy Jacobs, and Howerton. Clerk roll call noted Commissioner Heidi Carter attending in an unofficial capacity and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns listed as alternate, with City Manager Wanda Page and Interim County Manager Claudia Hager also present. One agenda item requested for removal by Charlie was postponed.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 12, 2021 Joint City-County Committee Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton called for a motion to approve the minutes from the October 12, 2021 Joint City-County Committee meeting. No corrections were offered, and both the county and city delegations approved the minutes unanimously by roll-call vote.

agenda_items.title: Bull City United Quarterly Update and Community Intervention and Support Services (CISS) Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Joanne Pierce presented the quarterly report under the city-county interlocal agreement, outlining the Cure Violence detect-interrupt-treat-mobilize model and Bull City United's expansion from seven positions in two census tracts (13.01 and 14.00) toward 25 total positions across six census tracts, with 16 onboarded and nine vacancies remaining. Pierce explained that Bull City United, Project BUILD, and My Brother's Keeper were consolidating into the new CISS department, highlighted an expected $250,000 federal grant and new Cure Violence Global database, and responded to elected officials' questions regarding hiring pace and outcome metrics.

agenda_items.title: Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Six-Month / Q2 Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Task Force Co-Chairs Marcia Owens and Xavier Cason reported on work across four roundtables covering violence interruption, non-police crisis response, school resource officers, and criminal legal reform, while raising concerns about Youth Home detention spending and Bull City United director vacancies. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and Chair Howerton criticized task force messaging and 'misinformation campaigns' outside the advisory bylaws, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and Council Member Freeman asked about overdue quarterly reports and communication protocols, and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson defended the task force's town halls and non-carceral focus.

agenda_items.title: Durham Children's Initiative Early Childhood Action Plan (ECAP) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After postponing the preceding scheduled item and agreeing to extend the meeting by 30 minutes past 11:00 a.m., the committee heard from Kate Elder, David Reese, Bonnie Dillon, and Joy Lampkin-Foster on Durham County's 18-month community-led Early Childhood Action Plan. Presenters and Council Member Freeman discussed opportunities for deeper city engagement, alignment with county ARPA investments, and cross-jurisdictional implementation ahead of the next joint committee meeting hosted by the City on February 8, 2022.

votes.item_title: Approval of October 12, 2021 Joint City-County Committee Minutes
votes.notes: BOCC committee roll call passed 3-0 (Allam, Jacobs, Howerton). City Council committee members DeDreana Freeman, Jillian Johnson, and Mayor Elaine O'Neal also voted Aye for a combined 6-0 joint committee tally. Mover and seconder not explicitly named in transcript audio.
votes.discussion_detail: No edits were proposed prior to the joint roll-call vote approving the October 12, 2021 committee minutes.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Meeting Oct 12, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 12, 2021 Joint City-County Committee meeting, Mayor Steve Schewel presided alongside Durham City Council members Jillian Johnson and DeDreana Freeman and Durham County Commissioners Brenda Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, and Nida Allam. The committee unanimously approved the minutes of the previous meeting and the 2022 Joint City-County meeting schedule on 6-0 roll-call votes. The bulk of the session focused on a presentation by Don't Waste Durham and the Duke Environmental Law and Policy Clinic advocating a 10-cent local retail fee on single-use carryout bags, countered by the North Carolina Retail Merchants Association's warning of state preemption under General Statutes 160A-215.1 and business burdens. Following questions about legal authority and legislative backlash—including DeDreana Freeman's concern over provoking state limits on local stormwater fees—the committee asked the City and County Attorneys to deliver a formal legal opinion before taking further action.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Approval of Minutes, and 2022 Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the Joint City-County Committee meeting to order with Council Members Jillian Johnson and DeDreana Freeman and County Commissioners Brenda Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, and Nida Allam present. With no corrections, the committee unanimously approved prior meeting minutes (6-0) and adopted the 2022 bi-monthly Joint City-County meeting calendar (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Proposed 10-Cent Single-Use Carryout Bag Fee Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Crystal Dreisbach (Don't Waste Durham) and Duke Environmental Law and Policy Clinic fellows presented a model ordinance imposing a 10-cent retailer-collected fee on plastic and paper single-use carryout bags (with SNAP/WIC exemptions and partial retailer retention) to reduce litter and stormwater infrastructure costs. Elizabeth Robinson (NC Retail Merchants Association) argued the fee constitutes an unauthorized local tax preempted by state law and burdens grocers, while committee members debated stormwater savings, small-business impact, and General Assembly backlash before requesting a formal legal opinion from the City and County Attorneys.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Referred to City and County Attorneys

meetings.title: April 13, 2021 - Joint City-County Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the April 13, 2021 Joint City-County Committee meeting, attended by BOCC Chair Howerton, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns alongside Mayor Steve Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, and City Council Member DeDreana Freeman. The committee unanimously approved the February 9, 2021 minutes 6-0 on a roll-call vote (BOCC Ayes: Howerton, Jacobs, Burns). Presenters from UNC Gillings and El Centro Hispano detailed the 11-member Back on the Bull Health Ambassador program's outreach to 986 local businesses and ~300 vaccine appointments for essential workers, sparking pointed discussion as Chair Howerton and Council Member Freeman pressed Mayor Schewel to coordinate his informal vaccine-equity stakeholder efforts directly with Public Health Director Rod Jenkins. The committee also reviewed reports on the Durham Small Business Recovery Fund ($1M+ in exhausted grants and $1.15M remaining in 3% unsecured loans, with Chair Howerton and Council Member Freeman requesting race-by-gender breakdowns) and the redesigned 480-participant Durham YouthWorks career-pathways program partnered with Durham Tech.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of February 9, 2021 Joint City-County Committee Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer confirmed a joint quorum comprising Mayor Steve Schewel, Council Member DeDreana Freeman, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, BOCC Chair Brenda A. Howerton, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns. Council Member Freeman moved approval of the February 9, 2021 minutes, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Johnson, and the motion passed 6-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: UNC Back on the Bull Health Ambassador Program and Vaccine Equity Coordination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Kurt Ribisl (UNC), Eliazar Posada (El Centro Hispano), and Dr. Patsy Polston reported that 11 community health ambassadors made 2,700+ visits, enrolled 986 businesses (including ~250 Black- and Latinx-owned businesses), distributed 30,000+ masks, and scheduled nearly 300 vaccine appointments (85% Black or Latinx). Committee members discussed demographic denominators, GIS mapping to avoid duplicating outreach, and Mayor Schewel's informal April 12 meeting with community groups on vaccine equity, with Chair Howerton and Council Member Freeman stressing the need to keep Public Health Director Rod Jenkins central and GM Joanne Pierce calling for explicit focus on structural racism.

agenda_items.title: Durham Small Business Recovery Fund Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Economic Development Officer Andrew Miracle, City OEWD Director Andre Pettigrew, and Carolina Small Business Development Fund CEO Kevin Dick reported that the joint City-County-Duke fund assisted 176 businesses with nearly $1.7 million ($1M+ in exhausted grants at 2/3 minority-owned and >50% women-owned; ~$1.15M remaining in 3% 10-year unsecured loans with 12-month deferral). Dick outlined proposals to rebrand the loan fund, raise the $35,000 cap, and allow refinancing of predatory loans, while Chair Howerton and Council Member Freeman requested disaggregated race-by-gender statistics for Black and Latina women-owned firms.

agenda_items.title: Durham YouthWorks Career Pathways Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City OEWD's Adrienne Graham-Scott, Durham Tech President JB Buxton, Candice Rashada, and Jennifer Fox presented the redesigned four-week hub-and-spoke Durham YouthWorks program serving 480 young adults (ages 16–24 across three 160-person sessions) with $559,500 in city funding and a $75,000 county pledge. By embedding Durham Tech coursework and virtual career simulations aligned with high-growth industries, the program aims to remove transportation and technology barriers, while Vice Chair Jacobs urged connecting youth to Durham College Promise and leveraging county economic incentive agreements for employer placements.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 9, 2021 Joint City-County Committee Minutes
votes.notes: Joint City-County Committee vote: BOCC members Brenda A. Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, and Nimasheena Burns voted Aye alongside City Council members Mayor Steve Schewel, Council Member DeDreana Freeman, and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson for a 6-0 committee tally (BOCC members Nida Allam and Heidi Carter are not on this joint committee).
votes.discussion_detail: Joint City-County Committee approved the February 9, 2021 meeting minutes without edits.
